report:
Reviewed the complete expand.dependencies claim, all six ordinary implementation entries, and the sole TODO test. Requirements: expansion may observe parsed identities, macro resolution/definitions, generated output and completeness; it must not consume checked signatures, trait solutions or function bodies. Captured modules design and architectural-foundations rationale for semantic dependency boundaries and coarse-input reexecution/backdating.

local_expanded_module_items is a tracked fixed-point query over module.unexpanded_items. Its helpers inspect item identities and syntactic attributes, resolve macro names, request parsed macro output and recursively expand generated items. Active-attribute and expansion-depth checks preserve incomplete expansion rather than invoking semantic checking. Resolver::new_for_macro_expansion creates an explicit expansion phase with module scope and fresh ribs; that phase combines named and glob lookup without normal-phase priority assumptions. Path lookup uses symbol/module identities; the captured symbol implementation's children method admits module/enum membership, not trait signatures or function bodies. The inspected resolver source has no signature, solver or body query calls.

LocalMacroInvocationSym::parse_output reads the invocation CST token input, asks the resolved macro definition for text, and passes generated text with source provenance/scope to parse_str_to_cst. MacroDefSymbol::expand reads local macro body tokens (macro definitions are allowed expansion input) or invokes external proc-macro expansion; these are not checked function bodies. DeriveExpansion::parse_output reads the tracked builtin output and parses it under source-item scope. expand_builtin_derive inspects supported struct CST shape, names and fields and writes ordinary Rust Clone impl text; it does not ask whether fields implement Clone or solve any trait. Later semantic queries assess generated implementations. Local derive resolution uses macro identity and is_builtin_derive metadata. The inspected derive and module helpers do not invoke sig/body/solve queries.

Captured parser entry creates CST/symbols from generated source through tree-sitter and parse_item_list. Captured LocalModItemSym attrs dispatch and LocalFnSym::attrs show the relevant distinction: expansion reads syntactic attributes through a coarse CST accessor, not the checked function body query. That may still produce extra execution after a source edit. This review does not assert that coarse CST input dependencies are already perfectly narrowed; the RFD distinguishes extra producer execution from semantic propagation and requires equal results to backdate. Symbol-only output and separate generated parsing boundaries support that design but do not prove its dynamic invalidation behavior.

The only associated test todo::modules_expand_dependencies has no assertions. It explicitly reserves cold/warm expansion traces, invalidation after invocation or selected macro-output changes, isolation from body-only/unrelated-signature edits, and backdating of unchanged reconstructed output before downstream execution. Completing it requires source-backed macro/derive fixtures, persistent database edits and query observations distinguishing allowed source reads from forbidden semantic calls. It should verify downstream reuse as well as producer execution, accounting honestly for current coarse source access. No ordinary runtime evidence is claimed from this placeholder; full semantic dependency and edit isolation coverage remains deferred.

Executed fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions, source and complete-test inspection, review read captures of modules design/RFD, parser entry and syntactic attribute helper dependencies. No tests or build run by this reviewer; central execution is separate evidence. No source edits or new suspected semantic-query dependency requiring reproduction. No requested edits, with the existing trace/invalidation matrix preserved as TODO.
